why: Telemetry for the pagination case, and the corpus's first whose two flat series are both correct readings rather than controls. A page that carries five lines instead of six is the whole of the evidence, and it is a count of things, so it is declared exact: a page does not carry 5.1 lines. The ratio at one is not a control -- every total really did reconcile, because the total is summed from the source list and the loop that lost the line is not on that path -- and the log count at zero is not a quiet log but an absent one: the loop skipped an item without evaluating a condition that could fail, so there is nothing for an error-rate reading to have missed. A corpus whose only moving reading is a line count is a case that a threshold on latency or on errors cannot solve at all.

series.quote: The invoice renderer skipped the last line of every multi-page invoice
series.why: the checkpoint `cp-lines-per-page` holds the five: both numbers are the case's own parameters, so the gap of one is the arithmetic the text states rather than two values edited into agreement
the checkpoint `cp-totals-match` holds the one: the total is summed from the source list, so it is correct and it is blind, and a reader who checks only the total concludes nothing is wrong
the checkpoint `cp-no-logs` holds the zero: the item was dropped without a condition that could fail, so the absence of a log line is the fault's shape rather than a gap in collection

noLogs: the text says nothing is logged and the totals still match, because a skipped line is not an error and the renderer had nothing to report.
noTraces: the work is a loop over pages rather than a call, and the chain stays inside the renderer, so there is no exchange to time.
